The Small Business Taxpayer Bill of Rights Act of 2025 (H.R. 2782) directly addresses systemic IRS overreach that’s crushed Main Street for decades. Section 6 bans ex parte communications between IRS appeals officers and enforcement staff—ending rigged audits. Section 3 raises civil penalties for IRS misconduct to $5M (from $1M), while Section 9 quadruples fines for unauthorized disclosures of taxpayer data. These reforms align with the NFIB’s optimism surge by slashing bureaucratic harassment.

But let’s be clear: permanent tax cuts and audit protections matter more than fleeting sentiment. Real progress requires locking in Section 14’s $5K deduction for audit expenses and Section 17’s repeal of partial payment demands during appeals.

Until D.C. stops weaponizing the tax code, optimism is just a talking point.
